question.knowledge_point: Integrating Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula for Cosine
question.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =4x,$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡8x={cos}^{2}⁡4x-{sin}^{2}⁡4x.
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}({sin}^{2}⁡4x-{cos}^{2}⁡4x)\text{d}x & =-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}({cos}^{2}⁡4x-{sin}^{2}⁡4x)\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡8x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡8x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\cdot 0)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}[\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0] \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}(0-0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
